newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria c.bank halted refinancing to banks in '97.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria c.bank halted refinancing to banks in '97.

text.p: The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) has halted refinancing to commercial banks since the beginning of the year as a step towards the introduction of a tough fixed exchange rate mechanism, a BNB official said.

"We have not extended loans to banks since the beginning of January and we will stick to this restrictive policy linked to the implementation of a currency board system," a BNB official, who declined to be named, told Reuters.
The total volume of loans extended by the BNB to commercial banks fell to 57.124 billion levs on February 21 from 62.336 billion levs at end-December 1996, BNB figures showed.
BNB Lombard loans to commercial banks stood at 1.0 billion levs on February 21, down from 6.257 billion levs at end-December and banks' overdraft decreased to 48 million levs from 107 million levs.

The central bank has also sharply pared refinancing to banks through its open market operations, halting revrepos longer than two days on January 20 as the Finance Ministry started issuing one- and four-week discount T-bills daily to drain excessive banks' liquidity.
The central bank also made no final purchases of treasury paper from commercial banks in the past three weeks.

The currency board system would require levs in circulation to be matched by central bank reserves, severely curbing the financial powers of the government and the central bank, thus preventing the printing of money.
BNB reserves stood at $445.5 million on February 28, up from $415 million a month earlier due to BNB net dollar purchases.
Senior government officials said on Thursday Bulgaria was likely to agree on a funding programme for implementation of a currency board system with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) next week.

IMF negotiators started talks with Bulgaria's interim government last week on a funding agreement linked to the introduction of a currency board mechanism to help stabilise the crumbling economy and repay foreign debts. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
